issueTitle: core:test: live E2E verification of the Gemini CLI runtime adapter

plan.summary: Verify the docs-derived Gemini CLI adapter (#243) against the real `gemini` binary: build a small, repeatable live-check harness (mirroring the existing `scripts/calibrate-confidence.ts` bundling pattern), drive a real coding run through `GeminiCliRuntime`/`runGeminiCodingAgent`, tick off every assumption in the issue checklist (stream field names, delta-vs-content duplication, MCP FQN prefix, flags, `.gemini/settings.json` lifecycle, resume, ENOENT parking), then land whatever one-line fixes the live run disproves and replace the "DOCS-ONLY FIXTURES" test data with a captured, redacted real stream.

ambiguities.detail: Which repo counts as a 'Gemini-selected repo' and what the actual coding task/prompt for the live run should be — the issue names no fixture repo or scenario
Auth method to use (Google login vs GEMINI_API_KEY) and how credentials are supplied/kept out of the repo

Whether verification evidence must be durably recorded (captured/redacted stream fixtures, pinned CLI version, new regression tests) or whether manual observation and ticking the checklist suffices — the plan commits to replacing the DOCS-ONLY fixtures and adding a pinned test, which the issue never asks for
Whether a reusable harness/script should be built (plan invents one mirroring scripts/calibrate-confidence.ts) versus ad-hoc manual runs
Which Gemini CLI version to verify against — the adapter was derived from v0.52.0 docs, but the issue's npm install pulls latest, leaving version pinning/reporting undefined
How far to go if an assumption is disproven beyond the anticipated 'one-line fix' (e.g. a structural stream-shape mismatch) — issue only excludes capability-matrix changes unless a fact is disproven
Whether an MCP server must be configured for the live run to observe a real mcp_<server>_<tool> name, and which one
How to simulate 'CLI missing' for the ENOENT negative check once the CLI is installed globally (PATH manipulation vs config override)

clarity.rationale: The issue is a well-scoped checklist of concrete, observable assertions against a real binary with explicit out-of-scope items, so done-ness is objectively checkable; the open decisions are mostly setup details (test repo, auth mode, evidence artifacts, version pinning) that the plan silently settled without flagging.

objections.detail: Step 3's `capture` mode hand-rebuilds the coding argv (`resolveGemini()` + `geminiBaseArgs()` + `--approval-mode=yolo` + `geminiSessionArgs(...)` + `buildGeminiProjectSettings(cwd).args`) instead of using the seam that already exists: `runGeminiCodingAgent(opts, spawnImpl)` takes an injectable spawn (packages/core/src/coder/gemini-run.ts:41, and the existing tests already exercise it that way). A hand-assembled command that drifts from gemini-run.ts:46-53 would verify a command Skipper never runs — the exact class of error this issue exists to eliminate. A tee'ing `spawnImpl` wrapper yields the raw NDJSON *and* the true argv in a single run, and collapses Step 2's five new barrel exports to at most one (`runGeminiCodingAgent`; `GeminiCliRuntime` is already exported from packages/core/src/index.ts:35), which also retires the plan's own "widens the public surface" risk.

Step 5's acceptance ("the memories-used card populates for the run") cannot be satisfied by the action it prescribes ("prompt the agent to search memory"). apps/desktop/src/orchestrator.ts:250-263 populates the card only from a tool-use whose `tool` ends in `__get_memory` AND carries a non-empty `detail` (the record id); search_memory calls are explicitly console-only ("search_memory queries surface only in the live console"). So the check requires a repo whose memory store already holds at least one record, a real desktop run (the harness cannot populate the card), and a prompt that pushes the agent from search to a full fetch. The plan also never says to build the `skipper.bundle.cjs` that `memoryServerConfig` requires (packages/core/src/llm/memory-mcp.ts:10-15) or to seed a record — without both, an empty card is ambiguous between "FQN translation broken" and "nothing to fetch", and the checklist item cannot honestly be ticked either way.

Step 5 enumerates the failure modes as "double underscore, dotted, or a server name that got mangled", all of which land in the `mcp_` branch at gemini-stream.ts:62-71. It omits the likeliest alternative: gemini exposing MCP tools under their bare names (`search_memory` / `get_memory`) or a non-`mcp_` scheme. That falls through `normalizeTool` to the `default` branch (gemini-stream.ts:91-93), emits tool `get_memory`, and silently fails the orchestrator's `endsWith("__get_memory")` test — a fix that lives outside the branch the plan points at and may need a server-name-aware mapping. Naming this outcome matters so it is not recorded as "prefix assumption holds, card just stayed empty".

The delta analysis in context item 2 is half wrong: "the fix is to ignore `content` on any line that also carried a `delta`" is already the behavior — `messageText` is `firstString(obj.delta, obj.content)` (gemini-stream.ts:98-100), so delta already wins on a line carrying both. Only the parenthetical (reset `pendingText` when a cumulative `content` arrives) is an actual change, and an implementer following the first formulation would ship a no-op and mark the assumption verified. The plan also does not enumerate the shape that hurts most: a stream emitting *only* cumulative `content` lines with no `delta` field, which the accumulator concatenates snapshot-on-snapshot (gemini-stream.ts:210-216) — while "replace on any content-only line" would silently drop text for a stream of non-cumulative `content` fragments. Step 4 should state which observation implies which of the three fixes.

The plan lists "committing raw, unredacted live captures" as out of scope and as a risk, but no step adds the ignore entry. `.gitignore` covers `scripts/dist/` and `scripts/calibration/runs/*/plans/` only — `scripts/gemini-live/` (the plan's own tee target) would appear in `git status` and is one `git add -A` away from committing prompts, absolute paths and repo content. Add the ignore entry in the same step that creates the harness.

The ENOENT check in Step 8 ("run with a PATH lacking it, after `invalidateResolvedGemini()` has a chance to re-resolve") misreads the resolver: on non-win32 `resolveGemini()` unconditionally returns `{ file: "gemini", argsPrefix: [] }` (gemini-cli.ts:45-49), so invalidation re-resolves to the identical value and the check is purely about spawn-time PATH. A subshell PATH edit also cannot affect a already-running Skipper — detectRuntimes and every spawn use the main process' PATH, fixed at app launch (apps/desktop/src/runtimes-ipc.ts:5-7). To exercise the desktop coder's park message you must rename the binary or relaunch the app under the stripped PATH; state which.

`packages/core/tests/fixtures/` does not exist today (verified: no files match), and Step 9 does not say how `gemini-live-capture.jsonl` is consumed — provenance-only artifact (in which case it is dead weight in the test tree, and the banner comment alone would do) or an actual test input (in which case the parse/assert wiring, and how redaction interacts with the assertions, needs specifying). Note also that `pnpm format:check` globs `{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md,yaml}`, so a `.jsonl` is unformatted/unchecked by the repo's own tooling.
